memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Moses took the bones of Joseph with him because Joseph had made the Israelites
swear an oath. He had said, 'God will surely come to your aid, and then you must
carry my bones up with you from this place.'" - Ex 13:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the quietest and most moving verses in the chapter.

Joseph died in Egypt around three hundred and sixty years earlier. Before he
died, he made his family swear to carry his bones out when God delivered them.
He said "God will surely come to your aid" as a matter of settled fact, though
he would not live to see one moment of it.

For three and a half centuries, someone kept that coffin. Through slavery,
through the bitter years, through generations who must have wondered whether the
promise had died with Joseph. Somebody remembered. Somebody passed it on.

And now, on the day of the exodus, in all the hurry and noise, Moses stops to
collect the bones of a man dead for centuries. Promise kept.

Hebrews lists this as an act of faith: "By faith Joseph, when his end was near,
spoke about the exodus of the Israelites from Egypt and gave instructions
concerning the burial of his bones" (Heb 11:22).

Joseph's faith outlived Joseph. What you believe and speak now may bear fruit
long after you are gone. You are permitted to plant things you will not harvest.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you doing now whose fruit you may never see?
2. Whose faithfulness are you living off today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, give me faith that looks beyond my own lifetime. Help me to be faithful
now, trusting You with what comes after me. Amen.
